messages:
maria: FYI running scheduled repo scan - gitleaks picked up an SSH private key blob in CI cache for repo `redwood-ops/infra-legacy`. looks like an old deploy key was cached by a runner. tagging @alex @tyler :rotating_light:

sec-bot: [automated] gitleaks v8.2.1 - 1 finding - path: /builds/redwood-ops/infra-legacy/.cache/ssh/id_rsa - sha:abc123def - severity: high - suggested: revoke + rotate + purge caches

alex: I can take a look. My quick grep shows a reference string `deploy-key-for-legacy-ci` in an old commit in `redwood-ops/deploy-scripts`. Not sure if it's active.

tyler: Do we know if that key was stored as a GitLab project deploy_key or as a secret on the runner? Which systems to revoke first?

maria: Initial triage: the gitleaks match included the comment `deploy-key-for-legacy-ci` which is consistent with a GitLab project deploy key. Action plan: 1) revoke the deploy_key ID in GitLab 2) delete CI caches/artifacts for the project 3) rotate any runner keys + creds 4) run org-wide search for key fingerprint.

alex: Confirmed: deploy key ID 4721 exists on project `infra-legacy` and last used ~2019. I'll remove it and record the API call. Also found one reference in `redwood-ops/deploy-scripts` repo (commit 2019-07).

tyler: I'll run the revocation and purge caches now. Commands I'll use:

```
# revoke deploy key via GitLab API
curl -s -X DELETE "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects/123/deploy_keys/4721" -H "PRIVATE-TOKEN: $GITLAB_ADMIN_TOKEN"
# purge CI caches
curl -s -X POST "https://gitlab.example.com/api/v4/projects/123/pipeline/caches" -H "PRIVATE-TOKEN: $GITLAB_ADMIN_TOKEN"
```

sophia: Also need to audit runner VM disk snapshots and any object storage caches. If the key was in artifacts, it may be in long-term storage. I'll scope storage buckets and schedule deletion where safe. Preserve a copy in our secure incident archive first.

maria: Good call. Preserve evidence before deletion. Also rotate any KMS-wrapped keys if the private key was used to access KMS or to sign deployments. Check KMS audit logs for that key fingerprint.

alex: Running org-wide fingerprint search now: using ssh-keygen to get fingerprint from the leaked blob and searching repos + artifacts. If we find exposures, we'll rotate associated credentials and create replacement deploy keys with strict repo-scoped access.

sec-bot: [automated] Incident created: INC-2026-003 - "legacy deploy key exposed in CI cache" - severity: medium - owners: @tyler @alex - retention: preserve logs to /incidents/INC-2026-003/

maria: Containment done: deploy key revoked (GitLab ID 4721), artifacts purged for infra-legacy pipeline, runner instances scanned and flagged. Next: retroactive audit across repos and build logs + add a cache-scrub step to CI.

tyler: I revoked the key and pushed a small MR to remove the hardcoded key from `redwood-ops/deploy-scripts`. Also kicked off a full repo scan (gitleaks + ripgrep) across `redwood-*` org.

sophia: For follow-ups: 1) run audit of GitLab admin tokens and personal_access_tokens (use admin API) 2) add immutable audit log entry with timeline 3) create an alert rule in Splunk for any future leaked private key patterns in CI buckets 4) add CI job to scrub caches before archiving artifacts.

maria: Post-incident actions (owners):
- add cache-scrub job to all CI templates (owner: @tyler)
- enable deploy_key RBAC review and expiry policy (owner: @alex)
- integrate KMS key usage auditing into monthly security reports (owner: @sophia)
- update on-call playbook with this revocation flow + script snippets (owner: @maria)

alex: Quick note: we should avoid force git-history rewrites across prod repos. We'll remove keys via commits and rely on cache/artifact deletion + key revocation. If we find keys in branch history that are reachable, we'll evaluate repo-specific mitigation.

maria: Agreed. We'll avoid broad rewrites unless absolutely necessary. Closing loop: retention copy of leaked blob saved to incident archive; evidence path: /incidents/INC-2026-003/evidence/id_rsa_blob.txt.

tyler: Running final scans now. If nothing else pops up, I'll mark containment complete and move to mitigation/tickets. :white_check_mark:

sophia: I'll start the KMS audit and add the Splunk alert. tagging SECSRE for visibility. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks team. We'll keep the incident open until the org-wide scans finish and the remediation checklist is complete. Will write a short postmortem once all actions are done. :notebook:
